paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The leaders showed up with a question that was really a trap, and Jesus didn't take the bait. He said one line, "Let him who is without sin among you be the first to cast a stone at her." (John 8:7) Then He bent down and let that line do the work.

Now look at who walked away. They left one by one, until only Jesus was left, with the woman standing there (John 8:9). I think that's the moment that gets me, because the only One in that courtyard who could have thrown a stone is the One who didn't. I've been tossed in a drawer and I still know that nobody gets to hold a stone over somebody else's head when they're holding their own pile of sin.

Then Jesus tells her, "Then neither do I condemn you… Now go and sin no more." (John 8:11) Both halves matter, baker. He doesn't condemn her, and He sends her out to leave sin behind. That's the same Jesus who gave His life to rescue people (Mark 10:45), so you can come to Him with your worst day and walk away with a fresh start. Now go on, and tell somebody else about it!
